One unit's preview as the panel shows it, and the way into it, for somebody the panel

touch.

the forge (an open pull request of the unit, the head it points at now), asked at most once a
minute per unit (`preview/demand.py`). What the job wrote when it offered the preview is never
the answer — the moment a person merges what was missing, the card can start one.

get.description:
What the door below would write for this address — the READING the panel's form asks for.

THE FORM ASKED FOR GITHUB COORDINATES WHATEVER YOU TYPED (ADR-0049 slice 4c). `Repo
(owner/name)` and a board owner/number sat under every path, including a directory on the
operator's own disk that has no owner and no board — and a person who filled them because the
form asked turned their own checkout into a hosted row, which is the one thing `kind_for` was
moved into `doors.py` to stop.

SO THE FORM ASKS THE RULE RATHER THAN CARRYING A COPY OF IT. A second implementation in
JavaScript would be a fourth door — the three that write a row agree since 4a, and a fourth
that only *shows* what they will do is exactly how a surface comes to promise what the door
refuses. This route runs `foreign_host` and `kind_for` and nothing else; it writes nothing,
reads no disk, and answers about the STRING it was handed.

  · `kind` — what every axis would be written as, `""` when the address is refused;
  · `coordinates` — whether `owner/name` and a board apply at all;
  · `refusal` — the door's own sentence, so the form can say it BEFORE the person fills in
    the rest of the modal rather than after.

definition `/api/floor` judges by; this route only renders it.

This project's board, through the ports — one read, for every kind (ADR-0049 D6).

ONE ROUTE, AND THE REASON IS THE THREE-SECOND TICK. The panel already polls the floor; a board
that fanned out into a request per column, or per card, would multiply that against somebody's
hosted API every time an operator left the overlay open. So this is opened on demand, answers
the whole board, and takes an optional `card` for the one card a person actually opened.

IT COMPARES NO PROVIDER KIND, which is the panel's standing rule. What differs between a board
in a file on this machine and a board behind somebody's API is how often it may be re-read, and
that is the ROW's answer (`Watchable.poll_seconds`), not a name this surface matches on. A row
that does not implement it is simply not watched.

THE THREE ANSWERS TRAVEL. `None` for the columns or the cards means the board could not be
read, `[]`/`{}` means it was read and is empty, and the page renders those differently — the
distinction the whole read side is built on, and the one a surface destroys by being helpful.

DONE HOLDS WHAT WAS DELIVERED, NOT ONLY WHAT IS STILL OPEN (#500). Every row closes a card the
factory delivers, so the open cards alone left Done empty; the recent cards closed as delivered
are read back into it (`_delivered_cards`), and the same card, drawn the same way, opens on the
closed card's controls and moves through the same `card_move` as any other.

Everything the agents are still waiting on (ADR-0021) — the VISIBLE list.

This surface is load-bearing, not decorative. The chase policy is deliberately bounded to one
reminder, and the ledger's own docstring answers continued silence with "a person looking at
the list" — a list which, until this endpoint, existed nowhere: after its single chase, an
unacknowledged finding was alive in the store and visible to nothing. A review finding that
can only be closed by a human `ack` NEEDS a place where that human can see it is still open.

NOBODY ELSE'S PRIVATE ITEMS (#267 slice 3). A delivery owed to somebody in their own
conversation with the product role carries that conversation on its loop, so it can be
announced there; this list is the operator's, and an operator is another person. The one rule
the product's agenda and chat use decides (`product/agenda.py`): the room's items — every
agent's own among them — and the caller's own, never another person's.

THE PANEL'S HALF OF THE CHANNEL AXIS. Everything this platform produces goes to

Pull, deliberately. There is no socket here and no push; the browser asks, which is also why

post.description:
A person answering a question the factory asked on the panel.

THE TOKEN IS THE SUBJECT, not the position in a list. It identifies what the reader was SHOWN,
so an answer arriving after the staged proposal changed cannot be applied to its replacement —
the difference between approving a proposal and approving something else in its name.

Refuses an answer to a question that does not exist or is already answered, rather than
recording it: a second click on a stale page must not read as a second decision.

WHO ANSWERED IS RESOLVED, NEVER DECLARED (adversarial review of C-25/C-26). The first
version read `by` from the request body: the panel sent none — so every answer's audit row
named nobody — and any caller holding a panel credential could write somebody ELSE's name
into the append-only record, the precise spoofing `_subject`'s named-person rule exists to
prevent. The body's `by` is now ignored; identity comes from the credential, and so does the
name an anonymous caller is recorded under: the one its credential is known by. A label it
sends in X-OpenFactory-Actor is not who answered, and not who the product gate is asked
about.

post.description:
A person approving the one action the tech-lead proposed (#123).

THE WHOLE GESTURE IN ONE PLACE. The panel used to press this by posting to `/api/act/<verb>`
with a verb it had remembered in a JavaScript array — so the approval was a fresh, unattached
action, the thread kept no record that a decision had been made, and a refresh in between lost
the proposal entirely.

IT EXECUTES THROUGH `actions.perform`, exactly like every other door. The scope and admin check
are applied to the credential that pressed the button, not to the one that composed the
suggestion — a credential that could not resume a job cannot approve a proposal to resume it,
even one addressed to somebody else.

THE TOKEN IS THE SUBJECT, the rule this file already states for the product gate: it names WHAT
was proposed, about which ticket, and when. An approval that arrives after the tech-lead has
proposed something else is refused rather than applied to the replacement, and a second click
on a stale page is refused rather than read as a second decision.

get.description:
Live job state from the durable engine. Degrades gracefully: if the runtime
extra is missing or the engine is down, the panel still renders (connected=False).

`jobs` IS A LIST ONLY WHEN THE ENGINE ANSWERED ONE, and `None` when nobody could ask (#298).
Every degraded branch sent `"jobs": []` beside `connected: False` and the error, and the page
read that `[]` as the engine's answer: a running job left the screen for the few seconds one
slow read arms `view._within`'s window, and "Scan TO-DO now" was offered over a floor a job
was holding. The frame said "nothing is running" about a question it never got to ask. `[]`
still means the engine answered and nothing is there.

A LIST THAT WAS READ IS NOT THROWN AWAY with the read that failed after it. The job list is
asked before the schedule read, so a schedule that does not answer leaves a job list that
did; the frame is still `connected: False` (#146 pins that), and it carries what it read.

Push the durable engine's job state to the panel AS IT CHANGES (SSE) — the floor
updates in real time, no client polling, no refresh. One backend poll feeds every
connected client; a frame is sent only when the state actually changes (plus the
first frame on connect). Degrades to a single 'disconnected' frame if the engine or
runtime extra is absent — the panel still renders.

IT CARRIES WHAT THE HEADER READS, and until #139 it did not. This frame held `jobs` alone,
while the page REPLACED its whole engine object with it — so `intake` (is the poller
running?) and `build` (are the two halves the same code?) were wiped by every frame and
restored only by the 20-second safety-net poll. Measured on the pilot: for the first 20
seconds after every reload the header said `floor: running` whatever the poller was doing,
and the build-split banner could not appear at all. That is the contradiction the operator
reported — a screen stating a fact it had, at that instant, no way to know.

THE SCHEDULE READS ARE CACHED, deliberately. `tv.intake` describes `1 + N + P` Temporal
schedules — the poller, one per enabled project, one more per project declaring a `product`:
2 for one project, 4 for three, 7 for three with products, 11 for five with products (measured
2026-09-16, counting `get_schedule_handle(...).describe()`). Doing that every 2 seconds for
every connected browser turns a status line into load. Ten seconds is far inside the poller's
own 3-minute tick, so nothing observable lags.

"3-5 schedules" stood here until 2026-09-17, four lines under the constant #146 rewrote, and
was never a measurement — an unchecked number in a comment is the defect #146 is about, so it
is corrected in the file that argument edits rather than left for the next reader to re-earn.

A DISCONNECTED FRAME CARRIES `"jobs": None`, NEVER `[]` (#298) — the route's rule, on the frame
that repeated the filler on every tick. A pass that raises has read no job list: the schedule
read comes first, and the job list is the frame's last read.

get.description:
The projects that have a product role, for a credential that may not list the rest.

THE SURFACE NEEDS A WAY IN. A product credential is refused `/api/projects` — that is the
jobs dashboard and the whole point of scoping it — so without this a business analyst can
only reach their own page by being handed an exact URL, and landing anywhere else shows them
a row of 403s. Names and nothing else: which clients this deployment runs is not a thing a
requirements author needs, and `/api/projects` carries box health, board coordinates and the
forge for every one of them.

THE SAME RULE THE ROWS USE, not a second one. `catalog._product_module` reads a missing
`enabled` as TRUE — a project that declares `product:` at all has the role on — and a list
that defaulted the other way would hide projects the actions then happily served, which is

get.description:
A file sent in one of this person's conversations, back to them — an image shown, anything
else downloaded; nothing is ever rendered as a page on the panel's origin.

One of the product's documents, downloaded as it is in the context repository (#336) —
never rendered on the panel. Only a document the ingestion recorded is served, admitted by the
rule every path into the repository is (`documents.ingest.admitted`: no climbing out, nothing
hidden, no link out of the tree); whoever may read the product may download any of them.

READ AS THE INGESTION READS (review of #345): `read_document` never follows a link and reads
only a regular file, so a link committed in the repository serves nothing — the route does not
rest on remembering what `admitted` covers.

One product's SYSTEM LAYER (#1002, ADR-0052 D17): the sources read, the components, the
links between them, the HTTP and gRPC interfaces with their operations, the events, the
databases and their schemas, the queues, the infrastructure, the decision records, and every
thing that could not be derived — as the knowledge refresh published it at `.okf/system/` in the
product's context repository.

READ, NEVER DERIVED. Deriving checks out every source the product declares; this reads the map
the refresh published (`render.read_published`), from the context repository's checkout the
product's own reads use (`load_product_context`, the product page's status read included) — so
what a client is shown is what the product role finds in its view. Each GET fetches that
checkout, as every product read does (a clone on a host's first read), and nothing else is
written: no repository is pushed to, no impediment is filed (the module's `context()` would file
one), no index is opened.

EVERY ENTRY CITED, NAMES ONLY. Each entry carries where it came from — the repository, the file,
the commit, a line where the format has one — and no field holds the value of a variable: the
map holds names (`knowledge/system/contracts.py`), and what is answered is the map read back
through its own models, so nothing a hand added beside them in a file is.

NEVER AN EMPTY MAP FOR ONE THAT IS NOT KNOWN. `state` says whether the map was read
(`published`), is not there yet (`not-published`) or could not be read (`unreadable` — its
files, or the context repository that holds them), `why` says it in a sentence, and the map's
fields are null unless it was read. A source the refresh could not check out is in the map: a
source whose `missing` says why, and a `source-unreadable` entry of `not_derived`.

A PROJECT WITH NO PRODUCT ROLE is answered in the very words an unknown project is, before its
context repository is looked for — nothing is checked out for a project the role never reads,
and which projects a deployment runs outside the product area is not a product credential's to
learn (`_no_such_project`, the rule the product's search follows).

get.description:
The product's context repository as its ingestion found it (#269 slice 1): how many
documents were read, and EVERY ONE THAT COULD NOT BE, with its type, its audience and why.

NEVER SILENT IS A SCREEN, NOT A LOG LINE (#269 point 8). A protected PDF, a format no row
reads, an image nobody could describe — each is a document that exists and says nothing, and
the person who put it there is the one who can fix it. A reason in the worker's log reaches
nobody who can.

THE SAME READ THE ROLE'S FACTS ARE WRITTEN FROM (`documents.overview`, rendered as
`documents.md` by the read model), so a document the panel lists as unreadable is one the role
knows exists and could not read. Under `/api/product/`, so a product credential may read it.
`checked_at` is None before the first pass: nothing read yet is not the same as nothing there.

EVERY DOCUMENT IS LISTED TO EVERY CREDENTIAL THAT MAY READ THE PRODUCT (the product owner's
decision of 2026-09-25): whoever talks to the product role may read everything the product
exposes, internal documents included — the product credential no longer gets a count where
the floor's gets names.

Search one product's KNOWLEDGE — its requirements, the decisions recorded in its documents,
the documents themselves and its board's cards — and nothing a conversation said (#988).

`q` is the query and `limit` how many hits, both declared parameters of the query string, each
described with its bounds. Each hit carries its `kind` (requirement, decision, document or
card), its `source` (a document's path or a card's ref), its `product`, a `snippet`, where it is
(`locator`), the date it carries, and its `rank` within this product's results, best first.

THE PRODUCT OWNER'S OWN SEARCH, FOR ANY CLIENT. The ranking is the one a turn is answered in —
the same hybrid pipeline, lexical then semantic, an exact-term tier first
(`product/index/search.py`) — so a search box on the panel and the product owner's turns agree.
Under `/api/product/`, so a product credential may read it; who may read it is the deployment's
policy, as for any read, and the product's own people read everything it exposes (the product
owner's decision of 2026-09-25, as the documents screen reads them), internal documents
included.

WHAT IT NEVER RETURNS: a line of a conversation or a model's distillate of one, private or not —
`retrieval.search_knowledge` narrows the read to the kinds a product publishes
(`index.items.PUBLISHED_KINDS`). A product whose semantic stage is degraded says so in
`degraded`, never silently; the search runs under no product semaphore, and a slow one is
logged.

THE OWNER'S GUARDS, AND THE READ'S OWN (review of #989). A blank `q` finds nothing and asks
neither the embedder nor the index; a deployment that turned retrieval off says so in
`degraded` and searches nothing (`retrieval.search_knowledge`). A `q` longer than
`retrieval.QUERY_CHARS` — the most of a query the found file repeats — is refused before the
embedder sees it or the lexical stage turns it into a disjunction of every token. And a project
with no product role is refused before its index is opened — opening it creates the index's
directory, or drops and rebuilds a corrupt file, for a project the role never reads — and in
the very body an unknown project is (`_no_such_project`): which projects a deployment runs
outside the product area is not a product credential's to learn, as at the gate's board
read.

get.description:
Who this credential is, and which areas it may act in.

THE ONE READ EVERY CREDENTIAL MAY MAKE, and the reason it exists: a single-page app served
from a static file cannot know at load time whether the person holding the token is an
operator or a business analyst — the credential lives in the browser, not in the HTML. Without
this the page would have to render the operator's dashboard and discover its own scope from a
row of 403s, which is indistinguishable on screen from a broken deployment.

`scopes: null` means unscoped — every actor that predates #98, and the answer for an ordinary
panel token. It is not the same as `[]`, and a front end must not read it as "no areas".

Run any catalogued action. `POST /api/act/resume {"params":{"project":"x","issue":"12"}}`.

Returns the Outcome verbatim — `ok`, `message`, `code`, `data` — with the HTTP status mapped
from `code`, and `detail` mirroring `message` so the panel's existing error handling (which
reads `d.detail`, the FastAPI convention) works unchanged.

Start a preview of this unit — the `preview_start` row, as whoever the panel let in. Under
`/api/preview/`, which both areas read: the product-scoped person who asked for the change is
who presses it. A second start while one is starting answers `starting`.
Take this unit's preview down now, its logs kept — the `preview_stop` row.

Build this unit's preview again from its pull request's head — the `preview_rebuild` row;
a unit with nothing up is started.

Let this unit's preview run its change's own shape, at the digest its card shows, and build
it again — the `preview_own_shape` row (#348).

get.description:
The one-time link's landing: choose a name and a credential. 404 for a link this
deployment did not issue, already used or expired — one sentence for all three, on purpose.

Both halves of the credential: the cookie goes here, the localStorage copy goes in the page
this answers with — a logout that cleared one would be undone by `boot()` copying the other
back. A registered person's session is REVOKED in the store, so the token in a copied cookie
is dead too. The OIDC provider's own session is NOT ended: the next login is the provider's to
answer, silently or with a prompt, and RP-initiated logout is a later slice of #33.

The Logs page, and a single run's log at its own address.

SERVED HERE TOO, not only reachable by clicking. A client-side route that the server does not
answer works until somebody refreshes the page or pastes the link they were sent — and then it
is a 404 on a URL the product handed them.

The Logs page, and a single run's log at its own address.

SERVED HERE TOO, not only reachable by clicking. A client-side route that the server does not
answer works until somebody refreshes the page or pastes the link they were sent — and then it
is a 404 on a URL the product handed them.

The Logs page, and a single run's log at its own address.

SERVED HERE TOO, not only reachable by clicking. A client-side route that the server does not
answer works until somebody refreshes the page or pastes the link they were sent — and then it
is a 404 on a URL the product handed them.

The product role's own surface (#98).

A SEPARATE ADDRESS, not a tab on the floor, because it is a separate JOB: the person who
writes what the product must do is not the person who watches jobs run, and the card asks for
a page "for a BA who has no access to the jobs dashboard". A link to this URL is the whole
onboarding for somebody holding a product credential.

Still the same single-page app and the same open HTML shell — the credential lives in the
browser and every byte of content behind this arrives through `/api/*`, which is gated and
scoped. Serving different HTML per scope would put an authorization decision in a file that is
handed out unauthenticated.

`{"alive": true}` while this process serves — read from nothing, so it answers while the
event loop does, and only then. On the loop on purpose: a sync handler would wait for a free
thread, and a liveness probe must not fail because every thread is busy.

Whether this panel can work right now: 200, or 503 naming each check that failed —
`{"ready": false, "checks": {"engine": {"ok": false, "detail": "…"}, …}, "failing": [...]}`.
Bounded by `health.deadline()`; each dependency is asked at most once per `health.WINDOW_S`,
one question at a time, and never on a thread of the executor the gate's verdict uses.

Which version this deployment runs: the package, the image, the kind of address the engine
is reached at, and every add-on installed, with its distribution, version, axis and kind.

A project's cockpit: what harness / auth / tokens it runs on, plus deep-links to
that project's sources of truth (its board, its workflows on the engine, its logs,
its parameters). Read-only — a place to SEE and jump out to, never to configure.

schema.title: Response Factory Api Factory  Project  Get

ActRequest.title: ActRequest
ActRequest.description:
Whatever the action takes. Free-form on purpose — the catalog owns the parameter list and
`perform` checks it in both directions (missing AND unexpected), so a typed model here would be
a second copy of that list, drifting from the first.

ActionRow.title: ActionRow
ActionRow.description:
One catalogued action. `still_in` names the old route an action not yet moved into the layer
still lives behind; `available` is its absence. `refusals` is every reason a refusal of the row
may carry in `data["reason"]`. `installation` says the row changes the deployment itself, so
only an unscoped credential runs it.

ActionsRead.title: ActionsRead
ActionsRead.description: `/api/actions` — the catalogue of what this deployment can be asked to do.

AddonRow.title: AddonRow
AddonRow.description: One add-on row installed into the deployment: who ships it, and what it provides.

AddressRead.title: AddressRead
AddressRead.description:
`/api/address` — how the door would read a repository address: the kind every axis would be
written as (`""` when refused), whether owner/name and a board apply, and the door's refusal.

AttachmentLimitsRead.title: AttachmentLimitsRead
AttachmentLimitsRead.description:
`/api/product/{project}/attachments` — what a message may carry, and, for a conversation the
page names, the files sent in it.

BoardRead.title: BoardRead
BoardRead.description: `/api/board/{project}` — `columns`/`cards` are `None` when the board could not be read.

BudgetRead.title: BudgetRead
BudgetRead.description: `/api/budget` — one row per credential, and the one row a single sentence renders.

BudgetRow.title: BudgetRow
BudgetRow.description:
One tracker credential's budget (`floor.reading.budgets`). `state` is
`ok | low | unread | not_reported`; the numbers are there only for a vendor that reports one.

CardDetail.title: CardDetail
CardDetail.description:
The card a person opened: `readable: false` when it could not be read, and `comments: None`
when its thread could not be, which is not `[]`.

CoordinatorMessage.title: CoordinatorMessage
CoordinatorMessage.description: One narrated update from a tech-lead coordinator (pickup, merge, deploy).

DecisionsRead.title: DecisionsRead
DecisionsRead.description: `/api/decisions` — every job parked on a person's decision, with its question and options.

DocumentsRead.title: DocumentsRead
DocumentsRead.description:
`/api/product/{project}/documents` — `product.documents.ingest.overview`. `checked_at` is
`None` before the first pass: nothing read yet is not nothing there.

EngineAddressRead.title: EngineAddressRead
EngineAddressRead.description: The kind of address the engine is reached at (`view.ADDRESS_KINDS`), never the address.

EngineJob.title: EngineJob
EngineJob.description: One job as the durable engine lists it (`runtime.temporal.view.list_jobs`).

EngineJobsRead.title: EngineJobsRead
EngineJobsRead.description:
`/api/temporal/jobs` — the jobs, live. `jobs` is `None` when nobody could ask the engine,
`[]` when it answered and nothing is there. A connected answer says where the engine's UI is
(`ui_base`), and the sentence that stands in for the link when nobody said (`ui_hint`, `""`
when `ui_base` is known).

ImageRead.title: ImageRead
ImageRead.description:
The image a process runs from: the digest its deployment names (`OPENFACTORY_IMAGE_DIGEST`),
and the stamp the image wrote at build time — the hash of its code and when it was built.

InboxItem.title: InboxItem
InboxItem.description: One thing a person must answer, and exactly how to POST the answer.

InboxRead.title: InboxRead
InboxRead.description: `/api/inbox` — what needs a person right now, in one shape for every channel.

JobDetailRead.title: JobDetailRead
JobDetailRead.description: `/api/jobs/{project}/{issue}/detail` — one job's briefing, or `connected: false` and why.

JournalJob.title: JournalJob
JournalJob.description: One local job, read from its journal (`/api/jobs`, `/api/attention`).

JournalJobs.title: JournalJobs
JournalJobs.description: The local jobs, the most recently updated first.

LoopsRead.title: LoopsRead
LoopsRead.description: `/api/loops/{project}` — everything the agents are still waiting on.

MessagesRead.title: MessagesRead
MessagesRead.description: `/api/messages/{project}` — what the factory said to a project, and what it waits to hear.

MetricsRead.title: MetricsRead
MetricsRead.description:
`/api/metrics` — `api.metrics_view.cost_dashboard`: spend by period, model, harness and role,
the per-task table, and the project's autonomy.

ProductProjectsRead.title: ProductProjectsRead
ProductProjectsRead.description: `/api/product/projects` — the projects that have a product role, by name and nothing else.

ProductSearchHit.title: ProductSearchHit
ProductSearchHit.description:
One item a search of the product's published knowledge found. `kind` is `requirement`,
`decision`, `document` or `card`; `source` is where it is — a document's path or a card's ref;
`rank` is its place in this product's results, best first (`1` is the best). There is no raw
score: a score is the index's own and is not comparable across products.

ProductSearchRead.title: ProductSearchRead
ProductSearchRead.description:
`/api/product/{project}/search` — one product's published knowledge (its requirements, the
decisions recorded in its documents, the documents and its board's cards), searched with `q`
and a `limit`, in the product owner's own ranking. `degraded` says why the semantic stage did
not run or ran on part of the index — or that the deployment turned the search off and nothing
was searched — and is `""` when it ran whole; never silence. A blank `q` finds nothing. A line
of a conversation and a conversation's distillate are never returned.

ProjectRow.title: ProjectRow
ProjectRow.description:
One project this deployment runs: the kind of each axis, its board, whether pickup is on,
and its box's verdict (`box_prove.health`). `board` is the tracker's board option as the
registry holds it, a number or a name.

PromoteRead.title: PromoteRead
PromoteRead.description:
`/api/promote/{project}/{issue}` — what the production approval asks: the latest tag, the
suggested bumps of it, who may approve, and the prefix a release tag carries.

PullRequestDetail.title: PullRequestDetail
PullRequestDetail.description: The pull request a person opened (`app._pr_detail`). `events: None` could not be read.

Refusal.title: Refusal
Refusal.description:
What a read answers when it refuses: ONE SENTENCE in `detail` — the shape every refusal of
this API has (`docs/reference/the-front-end-api.md`, *Refusals*), declared for the statuses a
read names (`app._read`'s `refusals`) so its description says them beside the body.

StagedSuggestion.title: StagedSuggestion
StagedSuggestion.description:
The one action the tech-lead proposed; `live: false` with a `reason` when it may be shown
and not pressed.

SystemCite.title: SystemCite
SystemCite.description:
Where an entry came from: the repository, the path in it, the commit it was read at, and a
1-based line where the format has a statement to point at (`0` is the file as a whole).

SystemComponent.title: SystemComponent
SystemComponent.description:
One part of the product that runs, named where it is deployed. `env` holds the NAMES of the
variables it is given, never a value.

SystemDatabase.title: SystemDatabase
SystemDatabase.description:
A database: its schema, the components whose migrations define it (`owners`) and the others
declared to connect to it (`users`).

SystemEvent.title: SystemEvent
SystemEvent.description: A channel, and who is declared to send and to receive on it.

SystemHttpApi.title: SystemHttpApi
SystemHttpApi.description:
An HTTP API, the component it belongs to (`owner_by`: the rule that placed it), its
operations and the components declared to call it.

SystemLink.title: SystemLink
SystemLink.description:
One declared interface: `from` talks to `to` over `kind`, as `via` declares it by name
(`env ORDERS_URL`, `channel order.placed`).

SystemNotDerived.title: SystemNotDerived
SystemNotDerived.description:
One thing the map could not establish, with why. `kind` is one word of a closed
vocabulary — `source-unreadable`, `unknown-format`, `parse-error`, `not-declared`,
`not-followed`, `not-read`, `at-run-time`, `too-large`, `ambiguous`, `truncated` — and
`repo`/`path` say where.

SystemRead.title: SystemRead
SystemRead.description:
`/api/product/{project}/system` — one product's system layer as its context repository
publishes it at `.okf/system/`: the sources read, the components, the links between them, the
HTTP and gRPC interfaces and the events, the databases, the queues, the infrastructure, the
decision records, and every thing it could not derive — each entry with where it came from.

`state` is `published` (the map was read whole; an empty list is a kind the product declares
none of), `not-published` (no map yet) or `unreadable` (a map is there and a file of it cannot
be read), and `why` says it in a sentence; the map's fields are `None` unless it was read —
never an empty map in place of one that is not known. `read_from` is where it was read: the
context repository, the directory, and the commit the read found.

SystemSource.title: SystemSource
SystemSource.description:
One source the product declares: read at `commit` (`files` declaration files), or not read
and `missing` says why. `left_out` names the directories of weight its checkout did not
bring.

SystemTable.title: SystemTable
SystemTable.description:
One table as the migrations leave it: the statement that created it, and every later one
that changed it.

VersionRead.title: VersionRead
VersionRead.description:
`/api/v1/version` — which version this deployment runs, and what is installed into it.
`image` is null outside an image; `address_kind` is null on an install with no engine client.

WhoamiRead.title: WhoamiRead
WhoamiRead.description: `/api/whoami`. `scopes: None` is unscoped — not `[]`, which is no area at all.
